props.title: All Together
lines: The book compresses into a short list of behaviours, not a formula.
Go out of your way to find humility when things are going well.

props.title: What to actually do
items: Go out of your way to find humility when things are going right, and forgiveness when they go wrong.
Less ego, more wealth: define enough; save; leave room for error.
Manage your money in a way that helps you sleep at night.
Increase your time horizon. Time is the most powerful force in investing, as Buffett's calendar showed.
Become OK with a lot of things going wrong. Tails drive the outcome.
Use money to gain control of your time. Avoid taking financial cues from people playing a different game.
Respect the fee: volatility. Pay it if you want the return. Be nicer and less extreme.

props.title: The behaviours again, slower
items: Humility in good times, forgiveness in bad. Outcomes mix luck into skill.
Define enough. Save more than is fashionable. Leave slack.
Sleep is a constraint. If the plan wrecks sleep, it will wreck compounding.
Lengthen the horizon. Buffett's calendar is the exhibit.
Accept that many things will fail. Own a wide enough net for the 4% and the 7%.
Buy time. Ignore players on another clock. Pay volatility if you want the return.

rows.v: When it is going well, hunt for the luck you are not crediting. That is how you stay kind.
When it is going badly, hunt for the risk that was always there. That is how you stay sane.
If the plan wrecks sleep, it will wreck compounding. Sleep is a financial constraint.
Become OK with a lot going wrong. Own a net wide enough for the four percent and the seven percent.
Volatility is the fee. Pay it if you want the return. Skip the product if you will not pay.
